proof_skeleton_nl: Introduce the auxiliary function H_{n,j}(d)=F_n(J_{n,j}(d)). First prove K_{n,j}(d)=H_{n,j}(d) on the admissible interval, then rewrite H_{n,j}(d) at an auxiliary x satisfying x=J_{n,j}(d). For the endpoint, specialize the interval identity at d=0, unfold H_{n,j}(0), and use J_{n,j}(0)=j/n. Finally conjoin the two resulting equalities.

steps.derives: For every real d with 0 <= d < 1/n and every real x with x = J_{n,j}(d), one has K_{n,j}(d) = F_n(x).
steps.trivial_justification: Instantiate L1 to get K_{n,j}(d)=H_{n,j}(d), instantiate L2 with the hypothesis x=J_{n,j}(d) to get H_{n,j}(d)=F_n(x), then use equality transitivity.

steps.derives: For every positive natural number n and every integer j, one has K_{n,j}(0) = H_{n,j}(0).
steps.trivial_justification: Use L3 to verify that d=0 satisfies the hypotheses 0 <= d and d < 1/n, then instantiate L1 at d=0.

steps.derives: For every positive natural number n and every integer j, one has K_{n,j}(0) = F_n(J_{n,j}(0)).
steps.trivial_justification: Combine K_{n,j}(0)=H_{n,j}(0) from A2 with H_{n,j}(0)=F_n(J_{n,j}(0)) from L5 by transitivity of equality.

steps.derives: For every positive natural number n and every integer j, one has K_{n,j}(0) = F_n(j/n).
steps.trivial_justification: From L4 obtain J_{n,j}(0)=j/n, and rewrite the right-hand side of A3 accordingly using equality substitution.

steps.derives: For every real d with 0 <= d < 1/n and every real x with x = J_{n,j}(d), one has K_{n,j}(d) = F_n(x), and moreover K_{n,j}(0) = F_n(j/n).
steps.trivial_justification: This is exactly the conjunction of the two derived claims, so conjunction introduction applies.
